questions.q: Three unrelated Scheduled Jobs all start degrading together, at the same start time, with no recent code changes to any of them. What does that pattern suggest, per this lab?
options: The reporting-refresh job's script must have broken and should be rewritten first
The instance's database has run out of storage space
Nothing meaningful can be concluded from that pattern
Semaphore contention — multiple jobs competing for the same limited background pool, rather than a bug in any one job's script
questions.explain: Multiple unrelated jobs degrading together, with no code changes behind any of them, is exactly the signature of contention for a shared resource, not a single broken script.

questions.q: Why is opening the reporting-refresh job's script and assuming it broke the wrong first move in this scenario?
options: ServiceNow scripts can never contain bugs
Reporting-refresh jobs are never allowed to run at midnight
Nothing about the symptom points specifically at that job's logic — all three jobs are affected together at the same start time
Scheduled Jobs cannot be edited once created
questions.explain: If the symptom were caused by one job's broken code, the other two unrelated jobs wouldn't be degrading at the same time for no reason.

questions.q: What is the practical fix applied in this lab to the three midnight jobs?
options: Stagger their start times across a wider window, such as midnight, 12:20 AM, and 12:40 AM
Delete two of the three jobs permanently
Rewrite all three jobs' scripts from scratch
Move all three jobs to run only once per month
questions.explain: Spacing out the start times reduces how many jobs compete for the same semaphore pool at the exact same instant, without touching any script.

questions.q: Why is Instance Health, not a single slow-transaction record, the right tool to confirm the fix worked?
options: Instance Health is the only tool capable of editing a Scheduled Job's start time
The Slow Request Log has been permanently disabled on this instance
A single slow-transaction record would actually be sufficient proof on its own
Confirming nightly processing is now reliable is a trend question across multiple nights, which is exactly what Instance Health is built to track
questions.explain: This directly applies Lesson 12's distinction: a trend across multiple nights is the right kind of evidence, not one isolated record.

questions.q: What is the real shape of the troubleshooting sequence this lab walks through?
options: Guess at a fix, apply it once, and move on without checking results
Only ever change one job's script, regardless of the actual cause
Recognize the symptom as instance-wide, diagnose it as contention, apply a practical fix, then confirm the fix worked over time
Immediately disable the entire instance until the problem resolves itself
questions.explain: Recognize, diagnose, fix, confirm — that four-step sequence is the practical pattern this whole chapter builds toward.
